items.title: Control must cover engineering decisions, not just file storage
items.summary: Assai DMS describes revision governance, approvals, transmittals and traceability across the asset lifecycle.
items.implication: Inference: measure correct, accountable issue and accepted information readiness; file-upload volume is insufficient.

items.title: Project acceptance and operating usability are separate checks
items.summary: Assai positions DMS across delivery, handover, operation and modification.
items.implication: Inference: require a receiving-team usability check and a reproducible accepted snapshot in the handover stream.

items.title: Approved changes can leave systems inconsistent
items.summary: Assai Enterprise explicitly describes engineering updates that are reflected in one system but missed in another.
items.implication: Inference: model each required downstream update with an owner and verified completion; approval or message delivery alone cannot close the change.

items.title: Asset context can span existing systems
items.summary: Viewport presents connected drawings, tags and operational information from existing systems.
items.implication: Inference: preserve source authority and support a standalone Viewport adoption path using external repositories.

items.title: Visible data gaps are part of useful retrieval
items.summary: Viewport describes identifying missing documentation, conflicting tag data and outdated drawings.
items.implication: Inference: assess association correctness, freshness and missing evidence alongside retrieval speed; route uncertain matches to a steward.

items.title: Parallel modifications require master protection
items.summary: Assai describes separate concurrent engineering copies, current-master checks and controlled return to operations.
items.implication: Inference: model explicit baselines and technical conflict resolution rather than treating parallel updates as ordinary file versioning.

items.title: Integration includes more than synchronous APIs
items.summary: Assai documents REST exchange, changed-data synchronization, Power BI extraction and scheduled FTP/shared-server publication.
items.implication: Inference: isolate connector contracts and observable reconciliation; legacy file exchange needs failure and freshness controls too.

items.title: Implementation should build customer independence
items.summary: Assai describes implementation progressing from vendor-led setup through joint work to customer ownership.
items.implication: Inference: measure practical first use and independent administration, and retain a customer-owned acceptance contract for cutover.

items.title: Complex project scope makes supplier participation consequential
items.summary: Assai publishes a DMS case focused on a global LNG megaproject and markets engineering document governance.
items.implication: Inference: an external supplier role needs clear deliverable obligations, scoped access and actionable rejection feedback. This role decomposition is proposed, not a reported interview finding.

items.title: Security assurance shapes technical evaluation
items.summary: Assai states that it maintains ISO/IEC 27001 certification, SOC 2 Type II attestation and CSA STAR disclosures.
items.implication: Inference: evaluate relevant assurance scope and customer-specific permission, recovery and export controls during procurement. No customer compliance result is inferred.

items.title: Investment context favors repeatable platform delivery
items.summary: Vortex reports a 2019 buyout, cloud modernization support and the 2024 viewport.ai acquisition.
items.implication: Inference: test reusable integrations and phased adoption across the combined offer; a common internal architecture or organization cannot be inferred from acquisition history.

items.title: Adoption evidence should remain scoped to its cohort
items.summary: Assai publishes a renewable-energy portfolio case emphasizing document-error reduction and user adoption.
items.implication: Inference: benchmark a new implementation with its own baseline and task-based activation measures; do not transfer a vendor case result into a universal KPI target.
